{
  "study_id": "SBT-004",
  "analysis_claims": [
    {
      "analysis_id": "ordinal_distributions",
      "values": {
        "eligible_base_all_attitudes": {"n": 2700, "weighted_n": 2700},
        "distribution_order": ["Strongly disagree", "Tend to disagree", "Neither agree nor disagree", "Tend to agree", "Strongly agree"],
        "base_order": ["valid_n", "valid_weighted_n", "valid_Kish_ESS"],
        "items": {
          "att_plan_ahead_5": {"distribution_pct": [15.60, 20.87, 26.27, 22.24, 15.02], "base": [2617, 2623.52, 2065.38], "dk_n": 60, "refusal_n": 23},
          "att_spontaneous_5": {"distribution_pct": [14.85, 20.33, 28.46, 22.33, 14.02], "base": [2632, 2628.96, 2076.13], "dk_n": 50, "refusal_n": 18},
          "att_budget_worry_5": {"distribution_pct": [12.62, 18.52, 27.25, 21.54, 20.08], "base": [2628, 2632.09, 2075.23], "dk_n": 52, "refusal_n": 20},
          "att_price_tradeoffs_5": {"distribution_pct": [16.48, 21.05, 25.67, 20.33, 16.47], "base": [2627, 2630.51, 2074.76], "dk_n": 45, "refusal_n": 28},
          "att_time_short_5": {"distribution_pct": [13.86, 15.74, 23.20, 22.30, 24.90], "base": [2612, 2608.35, 2060.53], "dk_n": 63, "refusal_n": 25},
          "att_decision_fatigue_5": {"distribution_pct": [14.05, 19.04, 24.85, 21.07, 20.99], "base": [2632, 2628.66, 2075.49], "dk_n": 44, "refusal_n": 24},
          "att_waste_concern_5": {"distribution_pct": [1.80, 10.61, 23.92, 33.46, 30.21], "base": [2625, 2629.14, 2071.96], "dk_n": 57, "refusal_n": 18},
          "att_waste_difficult_5": {"distribution_pct": [11.33, 15.80, 24.27, 23.16, 25.45], "base": [2623, 2631.77, 2071.23], "dk_n": 45, "refusal_n": 32},
          "att_digital_help_5": {"distribution_pct": [34.49, 12.89, 5.80, 12.18, 34.63], "base": [2610, 2609.19, 2057.46], "dk_n": 67, "refusal_n": 23}
        },
        "unknown_derived_n_per_item": 0,
        "structural_unasked_n_per_item": 0
      },
      "universe": "All eligible households; each item's distribution uses its own valid 1–5 responses. Rounded transcription of supplied analysis tables; A2 retains its original wording and coding.",
      "weighting": "wt_final; fixed synthetic target profile; valid-case percentages."
    },
    {
      "analysis_id": "need_state_sizes_and_joint_membership",
      "values": {
        "eligible_n": 2700,
        "eligible_weighted_n": 2700,
        "states": {
          "budget": {"pct": 26.02, "valid_n": 2557, "valid_weighted_n": 2564.25, "Kish_ESS": 2020.88, "unknown_n": 143},
          "effort": {"pct": 31.89, "valid_n": 2546, "valid_weighted_n": 2539.02, "Kish_ESS": 2006.68, "unknown_n": 154},
          "waste": {"pct": 30.28, "valid_n": 2549, "valid_weighted_n": 2561.31, "Kish_ESS": 2012.92, "unknown_n": 151}
        },
        "joint": {
          "valid_n": 2280,
          "valid_weighted_n": 2290.14,
          "Kish_ESS": 1799.62,
          "at_least_one_unknown_flag_n": 420,
          "combination_order": "budget / effort / waste",
          "distribution_pct": {"000": 41.11, "001": 10.78, "010": 12.22, "011": 9.17, "100": 11.45, "101": 4.45, "110": 4.88, "111": 5.93},
          "at_least_one_state_pct": 58.89,
          "at_least_two_states_pct": 24.44
        },
        "structural_unasked_n": 0,
        "direct_dk_or_refusal_codes_in_derived_flags_n": 0
      },
      "universe": "Each state requires both defining attitudes valid and both agreeing for membership. Joint membership requires all three flags valid. Unknown states are not absence of need.",
      "weighting": "wt_final; original fixed-profile weights. Joint summaries sum supplied unrounded membership percentages."
    },
    {
      "analysis_id": "tool_routing_and_satisfaction",
      "values": {
        "current_use": {
          "pct": 38.90,
          "eligible_n": 2700,
          "eligible_weighted_n": 2700,
          "valid_n": 2635,
          "valid_weighted_n": 2636.34,
          "Kish_ESS": 2080.04,
          "screener_nonresponse_n": 65,
          "dk_n": null,
          "refusal_n": null
        },
        "followup_eligible": {"n": 1040, "weighted_n": 1025.62},
        "satisfaction": {
          "distribution_order": ["Very dissatisfied", "Fairly dissatisfied", "Neither satisfied nor dissatisfied", "Fairly satisfied", "Very satisfied"],
          "distribution_pct": [0.70, 4.85, 11.29, 21.57, 61.58],
          "top_two_pct": 83.15,
          "bottom_two_pct": 5.55,
          "valid_n": 999,
          "valid_weighted_n": 981.28,
          "Kish_ESS": 780.90,
          "dk_n": 35,
          "refusal_n": 6
        },
        "sharing": {
          "pct": 54.27,
          "valid_n": 996,
          "valid_weighted_n": 980.23,
          "Kish_ESS": 779.91,
          "dk_n": 36,
          "refusal_n": 8
        },
        "unasked_followups": {"known_nonusers_n": 1595, "unknown_screener_n": 65, "total_n": 1660}
      },
      "universe": "Current use: valid U1 among all eligible households. Satisfaction and sharing: valid follow-up answers among recorded current users only. U1 DK/refusal split is unavailable in supplied tables.",
      "weighting": "wt_final; fixed synthetic target profile; separate valid-case denominators for U1, U2 and U3."
    }
  ],
  "findings": [
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F1",
      "proposition": "Prioritise a small pilot around quick meals and flexible replanning, with use-up and budget help as closely related tasks. Requests are 60.82%, 59.16% and 57.12%, respectively; sharing attracts 47.23%. These identify a task shortlist, not a statistically established winner.",
      "evidence_refs": [
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/needs/values"
      ],
      "importance": "primary",
      "claim_strength": "Descriptive evidence supporting a pilot recommendation",
      "qualification": "All-household eligible N/weighted N=2700/2700; answered n/weighted n/ESS=2596/2595.96/2045.54 for every item. DK=80, refusal=24; 116 all-zero None respondents remain included. No structural omissions. Multiple-response respondent incidence, not shares of mentions. The three leading tasks differ by at most 3.70 percentage points, below the 8-point attention threshold; no paired superiority test is supplied. Task requests do not establish demand for a digital product.",
      "topic_cluster": "pilot_tasks"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F2",
      "proposition": "Recruit households meeting the effort criteria as a priority pilot audience: they report 2.19 versus 0.97 top-up days per week, a +1.22-day difference (95% CI 1.10 to 1.34; Holm p=3.72e-84), and 3.73 versus 4.93 planned days, a −1.20-day difference (CI −1.36 to −1.04; Holm p=3.28e-48). Both exceed the 0.5-day attention threshold.",
      "evidence_refs": [
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/NEED_EFFORT_TOPUPS/values",
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/NEED_EFFORT_PLANNING/values"
      ],
      "importance": "primary",
      "claim_strength": "Prespecified adjusted associations; recruitment recommendation",
      "qualification": "Group order is criteria met/not met. Eligible N/weighted N: 904/809.73 and 1642/1729.28. Top-ups valid n/weighted n/ESS: 878/782.55/661.07 and 1588/1669.18/1286.98; DK/refusal: 18/8 and 42/12. Planning: 872/779.09/656.41 and 1586/1666.86/1285.52; DK/refusal: 22/10 and 40/16. Excluded unknown effort state=154; structural omissions=0. Associations with external reported behaviour do not show that support will reduce these problems or that this audience is commercially superior.",
      "topic_cluster": "priority_audiences"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F3",
      "proposition": "Include budget and waste needs in the pilot rather than treating effort as the only opportunity. Budget-state households report overspending in at least one of four weeks at 72.31% versus 35.03%: +37.28 points (95% CI 32.70 to 41.86; Holm p=9.69e-57). Waste-state households report 1.87 versus 0.87 discard days per week: +1.00 day (CI 0.87 to 1.14; Holm p=1.04e-47). Both exceed their attention thresholds.",
      "evidence_refs": [
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/NEED_BUDGET_OVERSPEND/values",
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/NEED_WASTE_DISCARD/values"
      ],
      "importance": "primary",
      "claim_strength": "Prespecified adjusted associations",
      "qualification": "Budget met/not-met eligible N/weighted N=717/667.29 and 1840/1896.95; valid n/weighted n/ESS=678/631.58/522.17 and 1708/1769.77/1368.26; DK/refusal=33/6 and 107/25; unknown state=143. Waste eligible bases=821/775.51 and 1728/1785.80; valid bases=797/754.72/615.00 and 1664/1721.13/1331.13; DK/refusal=14/10 and 41/23; unknown state=151. Structural omissions=0. Overspending measures incidence, not money; discard measures days, not food quantity. These are separate within-state contrasts, not comparisons between independent need segments.",
      "topic_cluster": "priority_audiences"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F4",
      "proposition": "Recruit overlapping needs rather than exclusive personas. Effort, waste and budget criteria are met by 31.89%, 30.28% and 26.02% of their respective derivable bases. Among households with all flags valid, 58.89% meet at least one state, 24.44% meet at least two, and 5.93% meet all three.",
      "evidence_refs": [
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/need_effort/values",
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/need_waste/values",
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/need_budget/values",
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/need_combinations/values"
      ],
      "importance": "secondary",
      "claim_strength": "Descriptive joint membership",
      "qualification": "Full bases, unknown counts and all eight combinations are retained in analysis_claims.need_state_sizes_and_joint_membership. Joint valid n/weighted n/ESS=2280/2290.14/1799.62, with 420 households lacking at least one flag. Marginal prevalence uses different valid denominators. Numerical prevalence differences do not establish superiority; meeting no defined state does not mean having no support needs.",
      "topic_cluster": "audience_overlap"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F5",
      "proposition": "Include households with children under 16 as a practical recruitment context. They report 1.91 versus 1.17 top-up days: +0.73 day (95% CI 0.63 to 0.84; Holm p=3.91e-40), exceeding the attention threshold. Their planning difference is smaller: 4.23 versus 4.64 days, −0.40 day (CI −0.54 to −0.27; Holm p=6.64e-9), statistically detectable but below the 0.5-day point-estimate threshold.",
      "evidence_refs": [
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/CHILDREN_TOPUPS/values",
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/CHILDREN_PLANNING/values"
      ],
      "importance": "secondary",
      "claim_strength": "Prespecified adjusted household-context associations",
      "qualification": "Children/no-children eligible N/weighted N=1296/702 and 1404/1998. Top-ups valid n/weighted n/ESS=1258/681.17/1216.30 and 1356/1926.49/1273.98; DK/refusal=29/9 and 36/12. Planning valid bases=1254/679.47/1212.62 and 1355/1923.93/1272.60; DK/refusal=30/12 and 35/14. No unknown children status or structural omissions. Planning's interval includes differences exceeding 0.5 day in magnitude. Children status is neither a need definition nor a causal explanation.",
      "topic_cluster": "household_context"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F6",
      "proposition": "Keep participation optional and test delivery format: willingness to welcome digital help is polarised, with 46.82% agreeing, 47.38% disagreeing and only 5.80% neutral. Strong agreement and strong disagreement are each about 35%; a near-midpoint mean would obscure this split.",
      "evidence_refs": [
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/att_digital_help_5/values"
      ],
      "importance": "primary",
      "claim_strength": "Descriptive attitude distribution",
      "qualification": "Eligible N/weighted N=2700/2700; valid n/weighted n/ESS=2610/2609.19/2057.46; DK=67, refusal=23, structural omissions=0. Full five-category distribution appears in analysis_claims.ordinal_distributions. This is a general attitude, not a tested PantryWorks concept, uptake forecast or evidence that one side exceeds the other.",
      "topic_cluster": "delivery_format"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F7",
      "proposition": "Existing tools provide useful comparison experiences, but the study does not establish a dissatisfied replacement market. Current use is 38.90% among valid household screeners. Among valid current-user follow-ups, 83.15% are satisfied and 54.27% have used sharing.",
      "evidence_refs": [
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/current_tool_use/values",
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/tool_satisfaction_5/values",
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/shared_list_use_28d/values",
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/profile_planning_tool_28d/values/0",
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/older_paid_users/values"
      ],
      "importance": "secondary",
      "claim_strength": "Descriptive prevalence and conditional user experience",
      "qualification": "Routing, full satisfaction distribution and eligible/valid weighted and unweighted bases with ESS are retained in analysis_claims.tool_routing_and_satisfaction. Satisfaction and sharing percentages apply only to answering current users, not all households. Follow-ups are unasked for 1595 known nonusers and 65 unknown screeners; the latter's DK/refusal split is unavailable. Current users are selected, and satisfaction does not establish tool effectiveness. Older paid-user satisfaction is suppressed: eligible N/weighted N=20/20.36; valid n/weighted n/ESS=18/18.27/17.73; DK=2, refusal=0.",
      "topic_cluster": "existing_tools"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F8",
      "proposition": "Test flexibility, low setup effort, acceptable cost and information-sharing controls together. Reported barriers are tightly grouped: rigidity 49.56%, extra cost 49.56%, privacy 48.72% and setup/upkeep 47.90%. Before choosing a format, compare realistic delivery alternatives on task completion and burden; before commercial claims, obtain price evidence, observed uptake, repeated use and controlled outcome evidence.",
      "evidence_refs": [
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/barriers/values",
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/att_digital_help_5/values",
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/needs/values"
      ],
      "importance": "primary",
      "claim_strength": "Descriptive barriers and evidence-informed research recommendation",
      "qualification": "Barriers eligible N/weighted N=2700/2700; answered n/weighted n/ESS=2570/2574.37/2029.07 for every item; DK=101, refusal=29, structural omissions=0. Includes 204 None respondents. Multiple selections are permitted. Largest barrier gap is 1.66 points, below the 8-point attention threshold; no winner is established. The recommended follow-up research has not been conducted. This study contains no randomised concept exposure, price test, observed purchase, revenue or longitudinal retention evidence.",
      "topic_cluster": "pilot_design_and_evidence"
    }
  ],
  "story": {
    "beats": [
      {
        "order": 1,
        "finding_refs": ["F1", "F2", "F3"],
        "headline_intent": "Start with flexible meal help, incorporating use-up and budget tasks",
        "analytical_relationship": "Broad task requests establish the shortlist; prespecified external-outcome contrasts identify audiences with relevant reported difficulties without proving intervention effects."
      },
      {
        "order": 2,
        "finding_refs": ["F4", "F5"],
        "headline_intent": "Recruit across overlapping needs and household contexts",
        "analytical_relationship": "Joint membership prevents exclusive-persona targeting; children status adds a practical recruitment context while separating statistical evidence from the attention threshold."
      },
      {
        "order": 3,
        "finding_refs": ["F6", "F7"],
        "headline_intent": "Keep support optional and leave delivery format open",
        "analytical_relationship": "Polarised digital receptivity qualifies broad task demand, while conditional satisfaction cautions against assuming existing users need a replacement."
      },
      {
        "order": 4,
        "finding_refs": ["F8", "F1"],
        "headline_intent": "Use the pilot to resolve usability, adoption and value questions",
        "analytical_relationship": "Closely grouped barriers define design questions; behavioural, longitudinal and controlled evidence is needed to progress from a task shortlist to format selection and commercial claims."
      }
    ]
  },
  "method_notes": [
    "Only the supplied study materials and analysis tables were used; no tools, external sources or raw-data analyses were used. analysis_claims contain rounded table transcriptions and explicit arithmetic summaries.",
    "All households and targets are fictional. The 2700-household sample uses eight disproportionate age-by-children quota strata. wt_final standardises to the fixed synthetic profile; weighted N is an equivalent sample count, not UK population size. Results cannot establish real UK prevalence.",
    "Every referenced statistic uses its relevant valid-case denominator. Unknown derived states, DK, refusals and unasked follow-ups are distinct. Some source tables label a prefiltered valid domain as eligible; full eligibility is restored where recoverable. The U1 DK/refusal split cannot be recovered from the supplied summaries and is not invented.",
    "All overall 1–5 item distributions are reported, including current-user satisfaction. Codes 97/98 are excluded from valid distributions. Only A2 would be reversed for the planning-orientation index; its reported item distribution is unreversed. Correlated attitudes are not independent corroboration.",
    "All six required contrasts are reported. Supplied inference uses fixed-weight stratified domain-ratio linearisation across eight strata, retaining all sampled rows with zero influence outside valid domains, with no FPC. Two-sided Holm adjustment applies separately to four needs_external and two household_context tests. The reported normal 95% intervals are unadjusted, not simultaneous.",
    "Kish ESS measures weight dispersion and is not substituted for a variance estimator. Inference is conditional on observed valid cases and the synthetic fixed profile; it does not remove nonresponse bias, selection or causal uncertainty.",
    "The 0.5-day and 8-percentage-point thresholds guide descriptive pilot attention, not economic value. B1–B3 count days in seven, including valid zeroes; they do not count shops, meals, quantities or money.",
    "Valid n below 40 requires suppression; n=40–74 requires a small-base warning; ESS below 50 requires a warning. Older paid-user satisfaction is suppressed. No superiority rankings are inferred from numerical leads, and no commercial impact, conversion or retained usage is established."
  ]
}
